title: Sales Enablement: Unified Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference covering: positioning and core messaging, competitive brief templates, a repeatable pitch deck outline, pricing guidance for prospects, representative case studies, and a customer-facing Security FAQ. Use this as the single source of truth for enterprise proposals, AE enablement, and presales engineering handoffs.

1) Positioning & Messaging (TL;DR)

- One-line positioning: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency LLM serving with production-grade controls for cost, reliability, and deployment flexibility.
- Key customer problems we solve:
  - Predictable latency and throughput for chat and generation workloads (SLO-driven serving).
  - Reduced per-token cost via batching, caching, and model/quantization recommendations.
  - Flexible deployment: hosted API for rapid adoption, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers.
- Core differentiators (talking points):
  - Production-first: observability, rollouts, and guardrails built-in (per-route dashboards, tracing, token-level cost breakdown).
  - Unified runtime across environments: same API and rollout model whether hosted or private.
  - Cost & performance controls: intelligent batching/caching, quantization profiles, and automated fallback policies.
  - Reliability: canary/A-B rollouts, automated fallback to smaller variants, multi-region failover.

Messaging pillars and example soundbites:
- Performance and predictability: "Ship LLM features without surprises — predictable latency, throughput, and unit cost."
- Cost economics: "Reduce token costs up to 30% through workload-aware batching and caching — not by sacrificing output quality."
- Flexible deployment: "Same developer API across hosted, dedicated, and private environments — control where your data and workloads run."
- Risk mitigation: "Built-in rollouts, observability, and compliance integrations for enterprise operational readiness."

Use-case tailoring: always start with the prospect's primary constraint (latency, cost, data residency, or SLA) and map to one of the deployment options + tooling that addresses it.

2) Competitive Briefs (one-page template)

Template sections (fill per-competitor):
- Competitor summary (1-2 sentences)
- Where they win (typical strengths)
- Where they lose (typical weaknesses)
- Common objections AEs will hear (with suggested rebuttals)
- Suggested positioning and differentiators to highlight
- Presales actions / demo checklist

Example: Competitor A — Large Cloud Provider Managed Endpoints
- Summary: Managed endpoint product from a hyperscaler that provisions model endpoints tied to cloud region and infra.
- Where they win:
  - Tight cloud provider integration and global availability.
  - Broad suite of other managed AI services.
- Where they lose:
  - Limited inference optimizations and no unified runtime across hosted/private.
  - Higher unit costs for latency-sensitive workloads due to lack of advanced batching/caching.
- Common objections & rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We already use Cloud X — why move?"
    - Rebuttal: "You can continue using Cloud X for your infra; Redwood layers at the inference runtime to reduce per-token cost and provide production controls unavailable in generic managed endpoints (detailed benchmark examples in appendix)."
  - Objection: "Model compatibility and handoffs will be messy."
    - Rebuttal: "Redwood's model catalog and rollout policies let you pin model versions and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback — we operationalize model upgrades."
- Suggested demo checklist: latency-vs-cost comparison, rollout demo, dedicated vs hosted decision flow, security checklist for Private deployment.

3) Pitch Deck Outline (recommended 12-16 slides)

1. Title / one-liner (logo, contact)
2. Customer context / prompt (pain + opportunity)
3. Redwood one-liner + key value props
4. How it works (high-level runtime + routing + caching)
5. Deployment options: hosted, Dedicated, Private (brief benefits table)
6. Reliability and SLOs: example metrics and monitoring controls
7. Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations with expected %s
8. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logging, SOC2/ISO roadmap
9. Case study snapshot (2-3 impact metrics)
10. Commercial proposal (pricing tier overview and optional add-ons)
11. Migration / onboarding plan (90-day plan with milestones)
12. TCO/ROI slide (example math)
13. Next steps / call to action

Deck best practices:
- Keep no more than 12-16 slides; each slide should have a single clear takeaway.
- Replace abstract claims with numbers and customer metrics where available.
- Have an appendix with architecture diagrams, benchmark charts, RLHF/eval examples.

4) Pricing Guidance (sales-facing)

Principles:
- Be transparent: provide sample unit economics so prospects can predict cost at scale.
- Tier by deployment and commitment: hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits), Private pricing (license + support + optional infra).
- Clearly list add-ons: extra observability retention, compliance package (SOC2/ISO evidence), premium SLA, professional services for on-prem packaging.

Suggested pricing bands (examples for prospect conversations — actual commercial quotes require finance approval):
- Hosted API (self-serve / small scale):
  - Text generation: $0.003 / 1k tokens (baseline model) — volume discounts at 250M+ tokens/month
  - Embeddings: $0.0008 / 1k tokens
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved):
  - Small commit (e.g., 1-2 vGPUs reserved): $12k / month baseline (example)
  - Medium commit (10-20 vGPUs): custom pricing with committed throughput SLAs
  - Enterprise: annual contract with reserved pools, burst options, and invoice terms
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Platform license + deployment fee + optional support tier. Example: $150k platform fee + $X/month support (custom).
- Add-ons:
  - Extended observability retention: $Y/month
  - Compliance evidence package (audit support): one-time $Z plus recurring fee for evidence retention

Pricing playbook for AEs:
1. Qualify for deployment mode early (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — it materially affects price structure.
2. Use sample math on slide to show expected monthly cost at target token volumes and latency SLAs.
3. Offer a 90-day pilot with consumption caps for evaluation; ensure pilot terms document responsibilities and success metrics.
4. For enterprise deals, involve solutions engineering early (by SDR/AE Stage 2).

5) Case Studies (two representative customer summaries)

Case Study: Acme Health — Clinical Triage Assistant (anonymized)
- Problem: On-prem clinical triage needed sub-200ms latency, strict PHI controls, and predictable monthly costs.
- Solution: Redwood Private deployed in customer VPC with model pinning, KV caching, and quantized model variant for inference.
- Impact (first 6 months):
  - Latency reduced from median 380ms to 180ms (53% improvement).
  - Inference cost per request decreased by 28% after batching and cache tuning.
  - Successful SOC2 audit for the triage service integration.
- Ownership: Solutions engineering + Private deployments team; on-call handoff documented in /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops.

Case Study: Breeze Commerce — Personalized Recommendations (hosted + Dedicated hybrid)
- Problem: Burst traffic during promotions required predictable throughput and cost containment.
- Solution: Dedicated reserved pool for peak windows + hosted overflow routing, automated batching, and prefix caching.
- Impact:
  - Reduced tail latency by 40% during peak loads.
  - Avoided 2.2x overprovisioning costs vs naive reserved-capacity approach.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers for presales)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: For Hosted API, data is stored in region you select and retained per our retention policy (default 30 days for logs, configurable for enterprise). For Dedicated and Private, data remains in your VPC or on-premises infrastructure.

Q: Do you provide encryption at rest and in transit?
A: Yes. All traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key control.

Q: What compliance certifications do you maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. ISO 27001 is on our roadmap; we provide customer-specific evidence packages for enterprise audits as an add-on.

Q: How do you support audit logging and access controls?
A: We provide per-tenant audit logs, role-based access control (RBAC), SSO integrations (SAML/SCIM), and token-level tracing for request attribution.

Q: Can we run Redwood in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes — our on-prem packaging supports air-gapped deployments with offline install artifacts and documented upgrade/rollback procedures. Engage Private deployments early to scope network and operational requirements.

Q: How do you protect model IP and customer prompts?
A: We separate model artifacts and customer data at the storage layer, support customer-managed keys, and restrict access via RBAC and audit logs. We also offer Private deployment where all artifacts remain inside the customer boundary.

Q: What is your incident response process?
A: We operate a 24/7 SRE on-call rotation with documented runbooks, customer incident SLAs for enterprise customers, and post-incident reviews posted to a secure incident channel. See /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process for details.

7) Objection Handling Cheat Sheet (common scenarios)

- "We already use X managed API": emphasize developer experience, cost/latency delta, and dedicated/private options for compliance. Offer to run a short perf/cost pilot.
- "We can self-host and save money": clarify total cost of ownership (engineering ops, SRE headcount, continuous kernel/optimization work) and offer an apples-to-apples TCO comparison.
- "How soon can we go to production?": provide a 90-day ramp with milestones and a funded pilot option for faster timelines.

8) Enablement & Presales Playbook (operational steps)

- Stage 0 (Discovery): qualify primary constraints (latency, cost, data residency, SLA). Owner: AE.
- Stage 1 (Solutioning): engage Solutions Engineering; pick deployment path and draft pilot success metrics. Owner: AE + SE.
- Stage 2 (Pilot): run 4-8 week pilot with defined KPIs (latency p50/p95, tokens/month, cost per 1k tokens). Owner: SE + Customer Eng.
- Stage 3 (Commercial): present commercial proposal, ramp plan, and support options. Owner: AE + Commercial Ops.
- Stage 4 (Onboarding): handoff to Customer Success and Eng Private/Dedicated teams for production rollout.
